source_text: Alia iam consuetudo inualuit. ieiunantes habita oratione cum fratribus subtrahunt osculum pacis, quod est signaculum ; orationis. quando autem magis conferenda cum fratribus pax est, nisi cum operantis oratio commendabilior ascendit, ut ipsi de nostra operatione participent, qua maduerint de sua pace fratri transigendo? quae oratio cum diuortio sancti osculi integra? quem domino officium facientem impedit pax? quale sacrificium est a quo sine pace disceditur? quaecumque oratio. sit, non erit potior praecepti obseruatione, quo iubemur ieiunia nostra celare. iam\' enim de abstinentia osculi agnoscimur ieiunantes. sed et si qua ratio est, ne tamen huic praecepto reus sis, potes domi, si forte, inter quos latere ieiunium in totum non datur, differre pacem. ubicumque autem alibi operationem tuam abscondere potes, debes meminisse praecepti; ita et disciplinae foris et consuetudini domi satisfacies. sic et die paschae., quo communis et quasi publica ieiunii religio est, merito deponimus osculum, nihil curantes de occultando quod cum omnibus faciamus.
thought_title: The kiss of peace on fast days
orientation: Tertullian is discussing the customs of prayer and now addresses the practice of withholding the kiss of peace on fast days.
pass_a_gloss: Another custom has now prevailed. Those who are fasting, after prayer has been held with the brothers, withdraw the kiss of peace, which is the seal of prayer. But when is peace more to be shared with the brothers, except when prayer, made more commendable by the one working, ascends, so that they themselves may share in our work, by which they may be moistened by their own peace in making peace with a brother? What prayer is complete with the separation of the holy kiss? What peace hinders the one doing service to the Lord? What sort of sacrifice is it from which one departs without peace? Whatever prayer it may be, it will not be better than the observance of the precept, by which we are commanded to hide our fasting. For now by abstaining from the kiss we are recognized as fasting. But even if there is some reason, nevertheless, so that you may not be guilty against this precept, you can at home, if perhaps, among whom it is not possible for the fasting to be hidden entirely, postpone the peace. But wherever else you can hide your work, you ought to remember the precept; thus you will satisfy both the teaching in public and the custom at home. So also on the day of the Passover, on which there is a common and as it were public religion of fasting, we rightly put aside the kiss, caring nothing about hiding what we do with everyone.

choices.why: The glossary requires this rendering for the fixed term.
Signaculum means a seal or mark of authentication; 'seal' preserves the metaphor of the kiss as confirming prayer.
The participle refers to the person performing the work of fasting; 'working' keeps the active sense.

choices.term: qua maduerint de sua pace fratri transigendo
choices.english: by which they may be moistened by their own peace in making peace with a brother
choices.why: The metaphor of being moistened or refreshed by peace is kept literally; 'transigendo' means settling or making peace.
rejected: by which they may be refreshed by their own peace in reconciling a brother

choices.why: Praeceptum refers to the Lord's command to hide fasting; 'observance' keeps the legal force.
Pascha refers to the Passover or Easter; 'day of the Passover' is literal and clear.

bible_refs.note: quo iubemur ieiunia nostra celare (by which we are commanded to hide our fasting)

pass_b_english: Another custom has now taken hold. Those who are fasting, after praying with the brothers, withhold the kiss of peace, which is the seal of prayer. When should peace be shared with the brothers more than when the prayer of the one working rises more commendably, so that they may share in our work, refreshed by the peace they made with a brother? What prayer is complete when separated from the kiss of peace? Whom does peace hinder while he serves the Lord? What kind of sacrifice is it from which people depart without peace? Whatever the prayer may be, it will not be better than observing the precept by which we are commanded to hide our fasting. For now we are recognized as fasting by abstaining from the kiss. But even if there is some reason, do not be guilty against this precept: you can, if necessary, postpone the peace at home, among those from whom your fasting cannot be entirely hidden. But wherever else you can hide your work, you should remember the precept. In this way you will satisfy the teaching in public and the custom at home. So also on the day of Easter, when fasting is a common and as it were public religious observance, we rightly set aside the kiss, not caring about hiding what we do together with everyone.

problems.why: glossary: banned rendering 'holy kiss' (use 'kiss of peace')
lint glossary: banned rendering of osculum pacis; use 'kiss of peace' ('holy kiss')

edits.old: What prayer is complete when separated from the holy kiss?
edits.new: What prayer is complete when separated from the kiss of peace?

fixed: The English used 'holy kiss' for 'osculum pacis', which the glossary bans; changed to 'kiss of peace' in the sentence 'What prayer is complete when separated from the holy kiss?' The other instance of 'kiss of peace' was already correct.

problems.quote: What peace hinders someone who is serving the Lord?
problems.source_quote: quem domino officium facientem impedit pax?
problems.why: 'quem' is accusative: 'whom does peace hinder while he serves the Lord?' Not 'what peace hinders someone.'
problems.fix: Whom does peace hinder while he serves the Lord?
problems.ruling: "quem ... impedit pax" has pax as subject, quem as object; English flips to "What peace hinders someone"

problems.quote: refreshed by their own peace in making peace with a brother
problems.source_quote: qua maduerunt de sua pace fratri transigendo
problems.why: 'maduerint' is subjunctive: 'may be refreshed' by the peace they made with a brother, not indicative 'refreshed.'
problems.fix: may they be refreshed by the peace they made with a brother
problems.ruling: "maduerint" is perfect subjunctive (may be refreshed); English uses indicative "refreshed"

edits.old: What peace hinders someone who is serving the Lord?
edits.new: Whom does peace hinder while he serves the Lord?

edits.old: refreshed by their own peace in making peace with a brother
edits.new: may they be refreshed by the peace they made with a brother

fixed: Changed 'What peace hinders someone who is serving the Lord?' to 'Whom does peace hinder while he serves the Lord?' because 'quem' is accusative and the sentence asks whom peace hinders, not what peace hinders someone.

Changed 'refreshed by their own peace in making peace with a brother' to 'may they be refreshed by the peace they made with a brother' because 'maduerint' is subjunctive, expressing a wish or possibility, not an indicative statement.

problems.quote: by which we are commanded to hide our fasting (Matthew 6:16-18)
problems.why: The source does not cite Matthew; the parenthetical citation is an unwarranted addition that changes the text.
problems.fix: by which we are commanded to hide our fasting
problems.ruling: Source 'quo iubemur ieiunia nostra celare' has no Matthew citation; adding '(Matthew 6:16-18)' inserts a reference not in the Latin text.

edits.old: by which we are commanded to hide our fasting (Matthew 6:16-18)
edits.new: by which we are commanded to hide our fasting

fixed: Removed the parenthetical citation (Matthew 6:16-18); the source 'quo iubemur ieiunia nostra celare' does not cite Matthew.

problems.quote: When should peace be shared with the brothers more than when prayer rises more commendably from the one working, so that they may share in our work, may they be refreshed by the peace they made with a brother?
problems.source_quote: quando autem magis conferenda cum fratribus pax est, nisi cum operantis oratio commendabilior ascendit, ut ipsi de nostra operatione participent, qua maduerint de sua pace fratri transigendo?
problems.why: English adds a comparative clause “more than when prayer rises more commendably” that is not present in the Latin; the original asks only when peace should be given to the brothers, unless the worker’s prayer is more commendable.
problems.fix: When peace is to be given more to the brothers, unless the prayer of the one who works is more commendable, that they may share in our work and be refreshed by the peace they have with a brother.

edits.old: When should peace be shared with the brothers more than when prayer rises more commendably from the one working, so that they may share in our work, may they be refreshed by the peace they made with a brother?
edits.new: When should peace be shared with the brothers more than when the prayer of the one working rises more commendably, so that they may share in our work, refreshed by the peace they made with a brother?

fixed: The English does add a comparative clause not in the Latin, but the Latin itself contains the comparative 'magis' and 'commendabilior', so the comparative sense is present. The real issue is that 'from the one working' misplaces the genitive 'operantis' (it modifies 'oratio', not the source of the rising). Changed to 'the prayer of the one working rises more commendably' to match 'operantis oratio commendabilior ascendit'.

last_rejected.quote: the prayer of the one working rises more commendably
last_rejected.why: Tertullian says the prayer of one who is fasting/working rises more commendably; 'the one working' loses the connection to the fasting context.
last_rejected.fix: the prayer of one who is at work rises more commendably
last_rejected.ruling: Latin says “operantis oratio commendabilior ascendit”; translation mirrors this literal wording.

polish.changed: Clarified that 'the day of the Passover' means Easter, not the Jewish Passover, and kept the kiss of peace terminology consistent throughout.

notes.quote: On days of fasting and on fast days
notes.why: Reader cannot tell if these are distinct categories or the same thing.
notes.fix: Use one term consistently, e.g. 'station days of fasting' vs. 'periods of fasting'.

notes.why: All three refer to the same ritual; reader may think 'peace' and 'kiss' are different things.
notes.fix: Use 'kiss of peace' consistently or gloss 'the peace' as 'the kiss of peace'.

notes.quote: on the day of the Passover
notes.why: Reader may not know Tertullian means Easter (Pascha), not the Jewish Passover.
notes.fix: Gloss: 'on the day of the Passover (i.e., Easter, the Christian Pascha)'.
